title: Generating proteins with computationally predicted functions and multiple states via multimodal diffusion - Nature Machine Intelligence
gist: MIT/UT-Austin researchers present ProDiT, a 321M–576M parameter diffusion transformer that denoises protein sequence (discrete masking) and Ca coordinates (Gaussian) jointly, trained on 128 million AlphaFoldDB/UniProtKB proteins with GO annotations. It matches RFdiffusion on structure generation at ~10x the throughput with a plain transformer (no equivariant modules), produces computationally predicted functional designs for 463 of 915 molecular-function GO terms, and introduces 'coupled structure diffusion' to design single sequences that scaffold two different motifs — demonstrated by calcium-switchable lysozyme and carbonic anhydrase active sites, all validated in silico only.

themes.theme: Multimodal diffusion beats specialized protein architectures

insights.claim: ProDiT, a 321-million-parameter plain diffusion transformer with no equivariant modules or two-dimensional tracks, matches RFdiffusion's protein structure-generation success rate and surpasses ESM3 (1.4 billion parameters) at every sequence length from 100 to 500 amino acids.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Evidence that generic transformer scaling is displacing hand-built geometric inductive biases in structural biology, shrinking the moat of specialized-architecture incumbents like RFdiffusion and ESM3.
insights.quote: Strikingly, ProDiT accomplishes all this with a ~5× smaller model than ESM3 (321 million versus 1.4 billion parameters) and without using any equivariant modules or two-dimensional tracks in its architecture.
insights.locator: Results — Multimodal generation of sequence and structure

insights.claim: A streamlined non-equivariant transformer architecture for protein structure diffusion delivers roughly 10x higher single-GPU throughput than RFdiffusion at all sequence lengths.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Order-of-magnitude cheaper sampling changes the economics of in silico design campaigns: screening breadth, not compute budget, becomes the binding constraint.
insights.quote: ProDiT exceeds the throughput of RFdiffusion on a single graphics processing unit by a factor of approximately 10× at all sequence lengths
insights.locator: Results — Multimodal generation of sequence and structure

insights.claim: Simpler architectures permit larger training crops (512 versus 256 residues), which the authors credit for the widening quality advantage over RFdiffusion on proteins longer than 300 amino acids.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Long-protein design (the commercially interesting enzyme regime) is where architecture simplicity compounds — watch which labs can train at 500+ residue context.
insights.locator: Results — "The difference in structure-generation quality is most substantial"

insights.claim: Performing diffusion directly in the native state spaces of sequence and structure outperforms multimodal approaches that discretize structure into tokens (ESM3) or embed sequence into a continuous space (ProteinGenerator).
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: A design-space verdict: tokenizing structure (the ESM3 bet) looks like a lossy shortcut, which matters for anyone underwriting token-based bio-foundation-model platforms.
insights.locator: Discussion — "In silico metrics of unconditional generation quality"

insights.claim: ProteinGenerator is largely unable to generate self-consistent sequence–structure pairs beyond 200 amino acids, whereas joint native-space diffusion succeeds at 500 amino acids under a strict scTM > 0.9 cut-off.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Concrete capability ceiling for continuous-sequence-embedding co-generation methods; length limits are the right technical due-diligence question to ask design startups.
insights.locator: Results — "For co-generation, ProDiT produces self-consistent sequence and structure pairs"

insights.claim: Independently sampling sequence and structure noise levels during training lets one model serve sequence generation, structure generation, inverse folding and co-generation without task-specific retraining.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Asynchronous multimodal denoising is a reusable recipe that collapses a toolchain of specialist models into one checkpoint — a cost and integration advantage for platform players.
insights.quote: At training time, the noise levels for sequence and structure are sampled independently; as a result, the model is able to denoise these modalities asynchronously
insights.locator: Results — Multimodal generation of sequence and structure

insights.claim: A single multimodal diffusion model matches the specialized inverse-folding model ProteinMPNN on sequence–structure self-consistency for its own generated backbones, while additionally supporting function conditioning that pure inverse-folding models structurally cannot.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Function-conditioned sequence design is the differentiator; backbone-only inverse folders become commodity components inside larger multimodal stacks.
insights.quote: inverse-folding models that predict sequences solely based on backbone structures, such as ProteinMPNN only optimize structural compatibility and lack the ability to be conditioned on function
insights.locator: Results — "This capability is crucial for function-conditioned generation"

insights.claim: Rosetta REF2015 relaxation shows that ProDiT co-generated and inverse-folded designs have energy-per-residue distributions similar to or more favourable than PDB monomers, indicating physical plausibility beyond pLDDT metrics.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Physics-based cross-checks are becoming table stakes for credible generative-design claims; absence of them is a red flag in competing papers.
insights.locator: Results — "We further assess the physical plausibility"

themes.theme: Function conditioning via Gene Ontology terms

insights.claim: Conditioning protein generation on molecular-function Gene Ontology terms yielded at least one computationally successful design for 463 of 915 tested GO terms, including terms present in under 0.01% of UniProtKB training examples.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Breadth of addressable function space, not single hero designs, is the new benchmark — track the 463/915 ratio as the metric competitors must beat.
insights.quote: In aggregate, 463 GO terms have at least one successful ProDiT design
insights.locator: Results — Steering design with molecular function

insights.claim: Function-conditioned generative protein design is data limited rather than capability limited: success rates track GO term prevalence in UniProtKB, falling for rare functions.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Annotation coverage, not model size, is the bottleneck — value accrues to owners of functional-annotation and assay data rather than to compute alone.
insights.quote: suggesting that ProDiT function-conditioned generation is data limited
insights.locator: Results — "In aggregate, 463 GO terms"

insights.claim: Classifier-free guidance, a technique imported from image diffusion models, raises functional success rate and sequence–structure self-consistency for low-success GO terms at the cost of diversity and novelty, and is not applicable to tokenized models such as ESM3.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: The image-generation toolkit transfers wholesale to biology for continuous-space models, giving them a compounding capability edge over token-based rivals.
insights.quote: We also build on techniques from image generative modelling for prompt adherence to further boost GO term adherence, a family of techniques not applicable to tokenized models such as ESM3.
insights.locator: Introduction / Results — Steering design with molecular function

insights.claim: High structural similarity combined with low sequence identity, long cited as proof of generalization in function-conditioned protein design, actually reveals memorization of structures through co-evolutionary constraints rather than structural generalization.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Reframes how to read competitors' generalization claims — demand most-novel-design statistics, not median TM-scores, before believing a design platform has escaped its training set.
insights.quote: however, this does not assess generalization across structures and instead reveals memorization of structures via co-evolutionary constraints
insights.locator: Results — "Previous work in function-conditioned protein generation"

insights.claim: Across 169 assessed GO terms the most novel successful design averages a TM-score of 0.64 to its closest AlphaFoldDB neighbour with the same function, preserving fold class while changing local structure substantially.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Quantifies how far generative models currently stray from nature — useful numeric anchor for IP novelty arguments around AI-designed proteins.
insights.locator: Results — "Although the median successful ProDiT generation"

insights.claim: Generations conditioned on common GO terms show better diversity than rare-term generations (0.60 versus 0.66 mean pairwise TM-score) while novelty versus AlphaFoldDB is essentially unchanged (0.81 versus 0.78).
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Rare-function design is not just lower-yield but also mode-collapsed; expect weak output variety exactly where unmet biological need is greatest.
insights.locator: Results — "We assess the diversity of the generations"

insights.claim: Multimodal function conditioning outperforms both inverse-folding generated backbones with ProteinMPNN and generating function-conditioned sequences alone, measured by DeepFRI-predicted functional success.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Supports the thesis that function lives in sequence and structure jointly — single-modality pipelines structurally under-deliver on functional hit rates.
insights.locator: Results — "Further supporting our hypothesis that multimodal reasoning"

insights.claim: Functional success in the study is defined solely by DeepFRI assigning the target GO term with greater than 50% confidence to an ESMFold-refolded structure, a predictor the authors concede may perform differently on synthetic versus natural proteins.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: The headline '463 GO terms' is a predictor-on-predictor result with no wet-lab validation — discount accordingly when pricing design-platform claims.
insights.quote: We acknowledge that DeepFRI may have variable performance on natural versus synthetic proteins and thus may have limitations.
insights.locator: Methods — Function conditioning

themes.theme: Active-site geometry recovery as functional evidence

insights.claim: A structural alignment pipeline filtering for 100% residue identity and sub-1-angstrom RMSD on annotated active-site residues found successful active-site geometry recoveries for 45 GO terms out of 337 screened.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: A stricter, mechanism-level success criterion than function-predictor confidence; 45/337 is the realistic yield figure for design campaigns targeting catalytic sites.
insights.locator: Results — "we found successful hits for 45 GO terms"

insights.claim: Validation of AI protein designs is bottlenecked by annotation scarcity: across GO terms, a median of just 0.23% of structures carry enough labelled active-site residues to be usable as alignment references.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Curated structural-function annotation is the scarce input in the whole stack — an underpriced asset relative to models and GPUs.
insights.quote: this pipeline is limited by the under-annotation of native active-site residues in UniProtKB
insights.locator: Results — "we developed a structural alignment pipeline"

insights.claim: A design conditioned only on aldehyde dehydrogenase [NAD(P)+] activity (GO:0004030) reproduced the active-site residues of betaine aldehyde dehydrogenase (PDB 1BPW) at 0.41 angstrom all-atom RMSD and conserved the Rossmann-fold NAD+ binding motif (Trp165, Asn166, Pro168, Lys189) at only 45% overall sequence identity.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Shows abstract functional labels can be translated into atomic-level cofactor-binding chemistry — the step needed before AI-designed enzymes become products.
insights.locator: Results — "We first present a generated protein conditioned on GO:0004030"

insights.claim: A malonyltransferase-conditioned design (GO:0016420) recapitulated catalytic Ser92 and His201 at 0.23 angstrom RMSD versus E. coli PDB 2G2Z plus the malonyl-CoA pocket topology, including the malonyl-carboxylate recognition Arg117 and oxyanion-hole Gln11, at 41% sequence identity.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Fatty-acid-biosynthesis enzymes are industrial workhorses; cofactor-pocket recovery at low sequence identity is the template for designing freedom-to-operate-clean enzyme variants.
insights.locator: Results — "We next showcase a generated protein conditioned on GO:0016420"

insights.claim: In both enzyme case studies sequence identity to the natural reference decreases with distance from the active site, meaning the model concentrates conservation where chemistry happens and diversifies the scaffold elsewhere.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: A reusable diagnostic for separating genuine functional learning from homology copying — apply it when reviewing any function-conditioned design claim.
insights.quote: the sequence identity between the generated protein and 1BPW decreases with distance from the active site
insights.locator: Results — Fig. 3 case studies

insights.claim: For native functions lacking GO annotations, the authors argue the recipe of labelling homologous sequences with a synthetic GO-style tag and tuning the model on it should extend functional co-generation to unannotated chemistry.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Implies the annotation bottleneck is partly soluble with bootstrapped labels — a cheap path for firms with proprietary assay data to create private conditioning vocabularies.
insights.locator: Results — "We expect that for native functions not covered"

themes.theme: Coupled structure diffusion for multistate and allosteric design

insights.claim: Coupled structure diffusion generates one protein sequence and two distinct structural scaffolds in a single generative rollout by running two structure-denoising trajectories, each conditioned on a different functional motif, against a shared sequence trajectory.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Opens designed conformational switching — the mechanistic basis for biosensors, molecular motors and inducible enzymes — without any new training data.
insights.quote: our protocol generates two separate structural scaffolds coupled to a common sequence in a single generative rollout
insights.locator: Introduction — "Leveraging ProDiT's multimodal capabilities"

insights.claim: Multistate protein design can be achieved with models trained only on single-state sequence–structure pairs, by factorizing the target joint density through a directed graphical model of the sequence–structure–function paradigm and sampling the product of single-structure conditionals.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Sidesteps the scarcity of structural-ensemble training data — a theory-side unlock that competitors can copy immediately, so the advantage is speed not exclusivity.
insights.quote: We circumvent this hurdle by formulating coupled structure diffusion, a principled technique for multistate design that requires models trained on only single-state sequence–structure pairs.
insights.locator: Results — Design of computationally predicted multistate allostery

insights.claim: The new sampling protocol replaces prior allosteric design approaches that fused domains together or exhaustively sampled alternative conformers with physics-based methods before searching for compatible sequences.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: A compute-heavy brute-force step in enzyme engineering pipelines becomes a single sampling pass — compresses design cycle times for controllable-enzyme programs.
insights.quote: our approach represents a major advance over previous protocols requiring brute-force sampling of plausible alternative conformations, previously thought necessary for such a protein design task
insights.locator: Introduction — "Leveraging ProDiT's multimodal capabilities"

insights.claim: A designed lysozyme scaffold places the substrate-recognition residue Trp108 at its native position when unbound but displaces it by about 15.3 angstroms upon calcium binding to an inserted 12-residue EF-hand motif from calmodulin, predicting disruption of the peptidoglycan binding cleft.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Demonstration case for ligand-switchable enzymes: the mechanism is amplitude-large enough to be assayable, so expect fast experimental follow-up attempts.
insights.locator: Results — "In our selected lysozyme scaffold"

insights.claim: A designed carbonic anhydrase scaffold reproduces the catalytic residues at 0.15 angstrom RMSD unbound, and calcium binding shifts the Thr199 hydroxyl by about 1.04 angstroms toward the zinc-coordinated hydroxide, which would competitively displace the nucleophile and block carbon dioxide hydration.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Carbonic anhydrase is already studied for carbon capture; switchable variants would add process control, making this a watch item for industrial-biotech carbon tech.
insights.locator: Results — "In our selected carbonic anhydrase scaffold"

insights.claim: Well-tempered metadynamics in OpenMM 8.2 (four walkers, 100 ns aggregate per condition) independently supports the switch mechanism, showing the active lysozyme conformation strongly destabilized on calcium binding with a roughly 10 angstrom Trp108 displacement at 20% occupancy and an intermediate 3 angstrom state at 80%.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Orthogonal physics simulation raises credibility above single-predictor evidence, but the 80% intermediate state signals the switch is partial rather than binary.
insights.locator: Results — "we ran well-tempered metadynamics (MetaD) simulations"

insights.claim: Both demonstration active sites were chosen because they are formed by contacts between sequence-noncontiguous segments, which the authors reasoned an inserted allosteric motif could disrupt upon effector binding.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Gives a selection rule for which natural enzymes are tractable targets for designed allosteric control — a screening heuristic for enzyme-engineering pipelines.
insights.locator: Results — "Both active sites are formed by contacts between non-contiguous segments"

insights.claim: Design yield for multistate switching is low and filter-dependent: 320 scaffolds were sampled per enzyme motif and only a subset passing simultaneous low active-site RMSD unbound, low EF-hand RMSD bound and self-consistent Chai-1 predictions were analysed.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: In silico hit rates for complex multistate specs remain thin; cost models for designed-switch programs should assume heavy oversampling and filtering.
insights.locator: Results — "We sample 320 designs for each active-site motif" / Methods — Multistate design

themes.theme: Training recipe, data strategy and compute

insights.claim: The training set is 128 million sequences filtered to pLDDT above 80 from the 214 million UniProtKB proteins with AlphaFoldDB structures, spanning 1.24 million FoldSeek clusters and 18.9 million MMseqs clusters.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Quantifies how predicted-structure databases have escaped the PDB's data ceiling — the scale argument that makes transformer-first protein models viable.
insights.locator: Methods — Data

insights.claim: Clustering training proteins by structural similarity rather than sequence similarity improved generation diversity, breaking with standard protein-language-model practice.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: A cheap, copyable data-curation lever that changes output diversity without touching model size — the kind of detail that explains quality gaps between similar-sized models.
insights.quote: we cluster proteins for training by structural similarity rather than sequence similarity; we found this to improve generation diversity
insights.locator: Methods — Data

insights.claim: Both ProDiT models were trained for roughly 500,000 steps at crop size 512 and 250,000–500,000 tokens per batch on only 16–32 NVIDIA H200 GPUs.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Frontier-class protein design remains reachable on tens of GPUs, so capability will diffuse to academic and small-cap biotech teams rather than concentrating in hyperscalers.
insights.locator: Methods — Model architecture and training

insights.claim: An unusually high 20% dropout rate in a 30-block adaLN-Zero diffusion transformer was found essential for protein sequence-generation performance.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Signals protein sequence diffusion is regularization-starved, not capacity-starved — a practical reproduction detail that separates working implementations from failed ones.
insights.quote: Unconventionally, we adopt a dropout rate of 20%, which we found essential for sequence-generation performance.
insights.locator: Methods — Model architecture and training

insights.claim: GO conditioning is trained with aggressive augmentation: terms are sampled in proportion to inverse frequency 85% of the time and dropped 15% of the time, with sequence or structure fully dropped 5% of the time each, while the 8,220-term vocabulary includes inferred parent terms.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: The inverse-frequency sampling and conditioning dropout are what make rare-function conditioning and classifier-free guidance possible at all — the implementation detail behind the headline results.
insights.locator: Methods — Model architecture and training / Data

insights.claim: Only 65% of UniProtKB entries carry at least one non-root molecular-function GO term, and those entries average 9.6 terms each.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Sizes the functional-label gap in the public protein corpus — roughly a third of proteins carry no usable function signal for conditioning.
insights.locator: Methods — Data

insights.claim: Structure is embedded with a plain linear layer on Ca coordinates with no geometric or equivariant transformations, which the authors frame as emerging best practice.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Confirms the field's drift away from equivariance; teams still investing heavily in geometric deep learning for protein generation may be optimizing a losing axis.
insights.quote: The structure is directly embedded with a linear layer without any geometric or equivariant transformations, following emerging best practice
insights.locator: Methods — Model architecture and training

insights.claim: Low-temperature annealed reverse diffusion, with stochasticity and temperature coefficients tuned differently for unconditional versus conditional sampling, is described as essential for generating high-quality protein structures.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Sampler tuning, not just weights, determines usable output quality — relevant to anyone evaluating open-weight protein models where defaults are unpublished.
insights.quote: As in previous work, we find these low temperature dynamics essential for generating high-quality structures
insights.locator: Methods — Continuous diffusion

insights.claim: The authors explicitly state that successfully scaffolding selected active-site residues does not guarantee catalytic activity, since sensitivity to motif placement error is unknown and second-shell or distal residues were excluded from conditioning.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: The honest limitation that gates valuation: every result here is computational proof of concept, with wet-lab activity and allostery still unverified.
insights.quote: We qualify that the successful scaffolding of residues selected for the active-site motif does not necessarily guarantee catalytic activity.
insights.locator: Results — end of multistate section

insights.claim: Large-scale multimodal training may reduce the field's reliance on specialized geometric architectures for protein modelling.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: If true, the scaling-and-data playbook from language and image models transfers to biology, favouring compute-and-data-rich entrants over architecture specialists.
insights.quote: suggesting that large-scale multimodal training may reduce reliance on specialized geometric architectures
insights.locator: Discussion

insights.claim: The authors foresee function-conditioned generations serving as new starting points for directed evolution rather than as finished proteins.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Positions generative design as a front-end to existing lab workflows — the near-term revenue model is seeding evolution campaigns, not replacing them.
insights.locator: Discussion — "In function-conditioned design, we foresee"

insights.claim: The authors name multistep enzymes, molecular motors and signalling proteins as the applications unlocked by combining multistate generation with atomic-motif and intramolecular-interaction conditioning.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Maps the next capability frontier for designed proteins — the categories where de novo design would create genuinely new product classes.
insights.locator: Discussion — "Coupled with our unique multistate generation capabilities"

insights.claim: Model code and weights are released publicly on GitHub with structural alignment data posted openly, continuing the pattern of frontier protein generative methods shipping as open artifacts.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Open release means no technical moat from the method itself; durable advantage must come from proprietary assay data or wet-lab execution.
insights.locator: Code availability / Data availability

insights.claim: Co-author Daniel J. Diaz discloses ownership of Intelligent Proteins LLC, consulting to biotech on AI protein engineering, and co-founding Metabologic AI, which develops commercial enzymes with AI.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Names a direct commercial vehicle translating this class of method into enzyme products — a concrete private-market touchpoint for the thesis.
insights.quote: D.J.D. is a co-founder of Metabologic AI, which focuses on developing commercial enzymes with AI.
insights.locator: Ethics declarations — Competing interests

insights.claim: The work was funded by NIH grants, the NSF AI Institute for Foundations of Machine Learning, the UT-Austin Center for Generative AI, a gift from Microsoft and DOE NERSC compute awards, with the research spanning MIT, UT Austin and the University of Washington Institute for Protein Design.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Shows public compute and corporate gifts, not venture capital, still underwrite the leading protein-design methods — relevant to policy risk and to where talent will be recruited from.
